question.text: If a PE fund shows a Gross IRR of 28% and a Net IRR of 20%, the difference primarily represents:

answer.text: Management fees, other fees, expenses, additional returns/carry, and applicable taxes deducted to move from gross to net

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines gross metrics as returns before management fees, other fees, expenses, and additional returns, and net metrics as including fees and carry, with pre-tax/post-tax variants. Its worked example shows fees, expenses, taxes, and carry moving gross to net. The Trap: Currency, volatility, and inflation adjustments are not the gross-to-net bridge. Only the listed deductions explain the gap between Gross IRR and Net IRR. Note: Earlier wording interpreted the 8% gap, labelled it "cost of intermediation," added a 7-10 year compounding example, and offered 4-5%/6-8% reasonable-gap thresholds. Those numeric benchmarks and labels are not directly supported by the checked workbook and have been removed; only the source-listed deductions remain.
